briefdescription.para: Maximum number of intermediate bytes collected during ESC/CSI sequences.

detaileddescription.para: Intermediate bytes occupy the range 0x20–0x2F and appear between the introducer and the final byte of an escape or CSI sequence. Four slots is more than sufficient for all standard VT sequences (most use zero or one).

briefdescription.para: Initial capacity of the OSC string hybrid buffer in bytes.

detaileddescription.para: OSC (Operating System Command) strings are terminated by BEL (0x07) or ST (ESC \). 512 bytes covers all practical title and clipboard payloads. The buffer grows geometrically beyond this initial size as needed.

briefdescription.para: VT command processor receiving all decoded semantic actions.

detaileddescription.para: All decoded actions are dispatched via direct method calls on this reference. Never accessed from the message thread during parsing.

simplesect.para: READER THREAD — all calls are on the reader thread.

briefdescription.para: O(1) state transition lookup table.

detaileddescription.para: Maps (ParserState, byte) → (nextState, Action). Built once in the constructor and never modified. Immutable after construction, so it is safe to read from any thread (though in practice only the reader thread calls get()).

briefdescription.para: Current state of the VT parser state machine.

detaileddescription.para: Starts at ParserState::ground. Updated by processTransition() on every byte that causes a state change. The state determines how subsequent bytes are interpreted.

briefdescription.para: CSI parameter accumulator for the current CSI sequence.

detaileddescription.para: Digits and separators are fed into this accumulator via handleParam(). csi.finalize() is called before video.applyCSI() to commit the last parameter. csi.reset() is called on entry to csiEntry state.

briefdescription.para: Buffer for intermediate bytes collected during ESC/CSI sequences.

detaileddescription.para: Intermediate bytes (0x20–0x2F) appear between the sequence introducer and the final byte. They qualify the meaning of the final byte (e.g. ESC ( B selects ASCII charset: intermediate = '(', final = 'B'). At most MAX_INTERMEDIATES bytes are stored; extras are discarded.

briefdescription.para: Number of valid bytes currently stored in intermediateBuffer.

detaileddescription.para: Reset to zero on entry to escape, csiEntry, and dcsEntry states. Incremented by the collect action handler.

briefdescription.para: Partial UTF-8 sequence accumulation buffer (null-terminated).

detaileddescription.para: As multi-byte UTF-8 sequences arrive byte-by-byte, continuation bytes are appended here. When utf8AccumulatorLength reaches the expected length (from expectedUTF8Length()), the codepoint is decoded and dispatched via video.print(). The buffer is 5 bytes: up to 4 UTF-8 bytes plus a null terminator.

briefdescription.para: Number of bytes currently stored in utf8Accumulator.

detaileddescription.para: Zero means no multi-byte sequence is in progress. When this equals expectedUTF8Length (utf8Accumulator[0]), the sequence is complete.

briefdescription.para: Hybrid OSC payload buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Lazy-allocated on first OSC sequence.

OSC strings are accumulated here byte-by-byte as oscPut actions arrive. When the OSC terminator (BEL or ST) is received, video.applyOSC() is called with a pointer to this buffer and oscBufferSize. The buffer is not null-terminated; oscBufferSize tracks the valid byte count. Starts unallocated and grows geometrically from OSC_BUFFER_CAPACITY on first use.

briefdescription.para: Number of valid bytes currently stored in oscBuffer.

detaileddescription.para: Reset to zero on entry to oscString state.

briefdescription.para: Allocated capacity of oscBuffer in bytes.

detaileddescription.para: Zero until the first OSC sequence is received. Doubles on overflow.

briefdescription.para: Hybrid DCS payload buffer (Sixel).

detaileddescription.para: Lazy-allocated on first DCS q sequence.

DCS passthrough bytes are accumulated here byte-by-byte as put actions arrive. When the DCS terminator (ST) is received, video.applyDCSPayload() is called with a pointer to this buffer and dcsBufferSize. Grows geometrically from 64 KB on first use.

briefdescription.para: Number of valid bytes currently stored in dcsBuffer.

detaileddescription.para: Reset to zero on entry to dcsEntry state.

briefdescription.para: Allocated capacity of dcsBuffer in bytes.

detaileddescription.para: Zero until the first DCS sequence is received. Doubles on overflow.

briefdescription.para: Hybrid APC payload buffer (Kitty).

detaileddescription.para: Lazy-allocated on first APC sequence.

APC passthrough bytes are accumulated here byte-by-byte as apcPut actions arrive. When the APC terminator (ST) is received, video.applyAPCPayload() is called with a pointer to this buffer and apcBufferSize. Grows geometrically from 64 KB on first use.

briefdescription.para: Number of valid bytes currently stored in apcBuffer.

detaileddescription.para: Reset to zero on entry to apcString state.

briefdescription.para: Allocated capacity of apcBuffer in bytes.

detaileddescription.para: Zero until the first APC sequence is received. Doubles on overflow.

briefdescription.para: Constructs the Parser and initialises the dispatch table.

detaileddescription.para: Constructs the Parser, binding it to a Video reference for direct action dispatch.

video
VT command processor. All decoded semantic actions (print, applyControlCode, applyCSI, …) are called directly on this reference on the reader thread.
MESSAGE THREAD — construction happens before the reader thread starts.
Stores a reference to video for use throughout the parsing lifetime. The DispatchTable member is default-constructed here, which populates the full (ParserState, byte) → Transition lookup table.

parameterdescription.para: VT command processor. All decoded semantic actions (print, applyControlCode, applyCSI, …) are called directly on this reference on the reader thread.

simplesect.para: MESSAGE THREAD — called before the reader thread starts.

briefdescription.para: Processes a block of raw bytes from the PTY.

detaileddescription.para: Processes a block of raw PTY bytes through the VT state machine.
This is the hot path. Each byte is looked up in the DispatchTable and routed to the appropriate action handler. The method processes the entire [data, data+length) range before returning.

data
Pointer to the first byte of the input buffer. Must not be null if length > 0.
length
Number of bytes to process. May be zero (no-op).
READER THREAD only. Must not be called concurrently.
This is the hot path. The method iterates over [data, data+length) and routes each byte through the DispatchTable to processTransition().

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the first byte of the input buffer. Must not be null when length > 0.
Number of bytes to process. Zero is a no-op.

simplesect.para: READER THREAD only. Must not be called concurrently.

briefdescription.para: Applies a state transition: exit action, transition action, entry action.

detaileddescription.para: Applies a state transition: exit action → transition action → entry action.

Called by process() for every byte that produces a non-trivial transition (i.e. state change or action). Performs the two-phase Williams model:
performAction (transition.action, byte).
performEntryAction (transition.nextState) if the state is changing.

byte
The input byte that triggered the transition.
transition
The (nextState, action) pair from the DispatchTable.
READER THREAD only.
performAction()
performEntryAction()
Implements the two-phase transition model for every byte that produces a non-trivial result:

listitem.para: Calls performAction (transition.action, byte) unconditionally.
If transition.nextState != currentState, calls performEntryAction (transition.nextState) to initialise the new state's accumulators, then updates currentState.

detaileddescription.para: When the state does not change (self-transition), only step 1 runs.

parameterdescription.para: The input byte that triggered the transition.
The {nextState, action} pair returned by dispatchTable.get().

briefdescription.para: Executes the action associated with a state transition.

detaileddescription.para: Executes the action associated with a state transition, calling Video methods directly for all semantic actions.

Dispatches to the appropriate handler based on action:
print → handlePrintByte()
execute → video.applyControlCode (byte)
collect → appends to intermediateBuffer
param → handleParam()
escDispatch → video.applyESC (…)
csiDispatch → video.applyCSI (…)
oscPut → appendToBuffer (oscBuffer, …)
oscEnd → video.applyOSC (…)
hook → video.storeDCSHeader (…)
put → appendToBuffer (dcsBuffer, …)
unhook → video.applyDCSPayload (…)
apcPut → appendToBuffer (apcBuffer, …)
apcEnd → video.applyAPCPayload (…)
ignore/none → no-op

action
The action to perform.
byte
The input byte associated with the action.
READER THREAD only.
Central dispatcher for all VT actions. Parser-owned accumulation actions (collect, param, put, oscPut, apcPut) are handled inline. All semantic terminal actions (applyControlCode, applyESC, applyCSI, applyOSC, storeDCSHeader, applyDCSPayload, applyAPCPayload) are called directly on video. handlePrintByte() remains on Parser and internally calls video.print().

parameterdescription.para: The action to perform, as determined by the DispatchTable.
The input byte associated with the action.

briefdescription.para: Handles a printable byte, routing it through UTF-8 accumulation.

detaileddescription.para: Routes a printable byte to video.print() directly or through UTF-8 accumulation.
If the byte is a single-byte ASCII character (0x20–0x7E), dispatches video.print() directly. Otherwise forwards to accumulateUTF8Byte() to begin or continue a multi-byte sequence.

byte
The printable input byte.
READER THREAD only.
accumulateUTF8Byte()
Called by performAction() for every action::print byte. Two paths:

listitem.para: ASCII (byte ≤ 0x7F): resets utf8AccumulatorLength to discard any in-progress multi-byte sequence, then calls video.print() directly with the codepoint value.
Non-ASCII (byte > 0x7F): delegates to accumulateUTF8Byte() to begin or continue a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence.

parameterdescription.para: The printable input byte (0x20–0x7E for ASCII, ≥ 0x80 for UTF-8).

briefdescription.para: Accumulates a byte into the UTF-8 sequence buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Accumulates a byte into the UTF-8 sequence buffer and decodes when complete.

Appends byte to utf8Accumulator. When the accumulated length equals expectedUTF8Length (utf8Accumulator[0]), the sequence is decoded to a Unicode codepoint and dispatched via video.print(). Invalid sequences (bad continuation bytes, overlong encodings) are silently discarded and the accumulator is reset.

byte
The next byte of the UTF-8 sequence (lead or continuation).
READER THREAD only.
expectedUTF8Length()
UTF-8 multi-byte sequences arrive one byte at a time from the PTY stream. This method maintains utf8Accumulator and utf8AccumulatorLength across successive calls:

listitem.para: Lead byte (≥ 0xC0): resets the accumulator and stores the byte at index 0.
Continuation byte (0x80–0xBF): appended to the accumulator if a sequence is in progress (utf8AccumulatorLength > 0) and the buffer is not full.

Completion check: after each append, if utf8AccumulatorLength equals expectedUTF8Length (utf8Accumulator[0]), the sequence is complete. juce::CharPointer_UTF8 decodes the null-terminated buffer to a Unicode codepoint, which is dispatched via video.print(). The accumulator is then reset.

detaileddescription.para: Invalid sequences (e.g. a continuation byte with no preceding lead byte, or a lead byte that interrupts an in-progress sequence) are silently discarded because the accumulator is only appended to when utf8AccumulatorLength > 0.

parameterdescription.para: The next byte of the UTF-8 sequence (lead or continuation).

briefdescription.para: Processes a CSI parameter byte (digit, semicolon, or colon).

detaileddescription.para: Feeds a CSI parameter byte into the CSI accumulator.

Feeds the byte into the csi accumulator:
'0'–'9' → csi.addDigit()
';' or ':' → csi.addSeparator()

byte
The parameter byte (0x30–0x3B range).
READER THREAD only.
CSI::addDigit()
CSI::addSeparator()
Called by performAction() for every action::param byte. The byte is classified and forwarded to the appropriate CSI method:

listitem.para: Digit ('0'–'9'): csi.addDigit (byte - '0') — extends the current numeric parameter.
Separator (';' or ':'): csi.addSeparator (byte) — commits the current parameter and begins the next. Colon (:) is used for sub-parameters in extended SGR colour sequences (e.g. 38:2:r:g:b).

parameterdescription.para: The parameter byte (0x30–0x3B range per the VT spec).

briefdescription.para: Performs the entry action for a newly entered parser state.

detaileddescription.para:
Called by processTransition() when the state changes. Entry actions reset state-specific accumulators:
csiEntry → csi.reset(), intermediateCount = 0
escape → intermediateCount = 0
oscString → oscBufferSize = 0
apcString → apcBufferSize = 0
dcsEntry → csi.reset(), intermediateCount = 0, dcsBufferSize = 0

newState
The state being entered.
READER THREAD only.
Called by processTransition() immediately after performAction() when the state changes. Entry actions reset the accumulators that belong to the new state, ensuring no stale data from a previous sequence leaks in:

listitem.para: escape — intermediateCount = 0: clears intermediate buffer for the new ESC sequence.
csiEntry — csi.reset() + intermediateCount = 0: clears both the CSI parameter accumulator and the intermediate buffer.
dcsEntry — same as csiEntry plus dcsBufferSize = 0: resets the DCS payload accumulator.
oscString — oscBufferSize = 0: clears the hybrid OSC payload buffer.
apcString — apcBufferSize = 0: clears the APC payload buffer.
All other states have no entry action (default branch is a no-op).

memberdef.name: appendToBuffer

briefdescription.para: Appends a byte to a hybrid buffer with lazy allocation and geometric growth.

detaileddescription.para: On first call (capacity == 0), allocates initialCapacity bytes. On subsequent overflow (size >= capacity), doubles the capacity. The existing contents are preserved across reallocations via std::memcpy.

buffer
The HeapBlock to append to.
size
Current number of valid bytes in buffer (in/out).
capacity
Current allocated capacity of buffer (in/out).
byte
The byte to append.
initialCapacity
Capacity to allocate on the first call.
READER THREAD only.
noexcept — allocation failure on the reader thread is unrecoverable; juce::HeapBlock::allocate asserts in debug builds.
Handles three cases:

listitem.para: First call (capacity == 0): allocates initialCapacity bytes via juce::HeapBlock::allocate.
Overflow (size >= capacity): doubles the capacity and copies the existing content to the new block via std::memcpy.
Normal (size < capacity): writes byte directly.

detaileddescription.para: After ensuring sufficient capacity, byte is stored at buffer[size] and size is incremented.

parameterdescription.para: Current number of valid bytes in buffer (in/out).
Capacity to allocate on the first call.

briefdescription.para: Returns the expected total byte length of a UTF-8 sequence from its lead byte.

detaileddescription.para:
leadByte
The first byte of the UTF-8 sequence.
Expected total byte count (1–4).
Pure function — no side effects.
READER THREAD only.
Decodes the sequence length from the high bits of the lead byte using the standard UTF-8 encoding rules:
Values in the range 0x80–0xBF (continuation bytes) are not valid lead bytes and return 1 as a safe fallback.

parameterdescription.para: The first byte of the UTF-8 sequence.

briefdescription.para: VT100/VT520 DFA byte decoder — decodes VT sequences and calls Video methods directly.

detaileddescription.para: Parser owns the DFA state, intermediate and parameter accumulators, UTF-8 accumulation, and OSC/DCS/APC payload buffers. It holds a reference to Video and calls every decoded semantic action directly on it — it does not write cells, move cursors, or touch any terminal state itself.

Feed raw PTY bytes via process() on the reader thread.
